newsitem.title: UK: EMU expectations remain high - JP Morgan calculator.
newsitem.headline: EMU expectations remain high - JP Morgan calculator.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based European monetary union remained high as the new year got underway, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.
In the past five trading days, market prices indicate that the perceived probability of Spain, Italy, Denmark and the UK joining EMU in 1999 all climbed.
Only Italy has recorded a net decline in the assigned probability of its joining EMU over the past 20 trading days. Probabilities in Spain and Sweden are both above 75 percent.
"Optimism that EMU will be a wide club remains high," JP Morgan analysts said in a note accompanying the calculator.
"Despite a shift to greater euroscepticism within the British cabinet, market expectations that the UK will participate in EMU have remained steady, if low," they said.
According to these calculations, the market still believes there is a 100 percent chance France and Belgium will be in EMU in 1999, unchanged from last week.

JP Morgan's EMU calculator derives from the interest rate swaps market probabilities of individual countries joining Germany in EMU in 1999. The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
